Independent security review reproduced High integrity failures in the proposed receipt design: callers can publicly build and self-register forged receipts/stores; stateful baseline containers can change between canonical digest and risk traversal (TOCTOU); MergeCommitReceiptStore can be directly constructed with duplicate or mutable receipts, bypassing register replay checks. Required redesign: non-forgeable authority boundary/attestation, strict deep immutable canonical domain validation with one frozen snapshot, and sealed store construction invariants.

Planner decision-required: existing PrivateKeyService/Windows helper supports non-exportable handle signing but has no verify operation or usable public key material. Minimum secure receipt verification requires adding a Verify action to the existing CNG helper and PrivateKeyStore/Service, binding certificate_id, pinned parent thumbprint and public digest, then updating the locked helper artifact size/hash and toolchain lock. Explicit owner approval is required before changing locked security tooling.

Independent security review reproduced three High failures in signed receipts: Risk accepts caller-supplied signing authority/trust pin; historical receipts are not all signature-verified and store snapshots can be truncated/replayed without a trusted current chain head; PrivateKeyService.revoke only returns metadata so stale references still sign/verify because backend revocation is not persisted. Required redesign: system-configured verification-only policy/repository, signed chained head with freshness/audit anchor and full-history verification, and backend atomic Revoke checked on every use/verify.

Planner decision-required: closing the latest High findings requires (1) backend atomic CNG Revoke/tombstone persisted by store_private_key.ps1/PrivateKeyStore so stale references fail every use/verify, with helper integrity lock update; and (2) a controlled project-state directory persisting receipt history/current-head using SignedAuditAnchor/WindowsFreshnessAuthority artifacts with explicit retention/recovery policy. These security lifecycle and persistent-state changes require explicit owner approval.

Independent protocol review found a ?16/?17 atomicity violation: MergeReceiptRepository commits SQLite and promotes the signed anchor before MergeEngine runs append_signed_receipt business-history validation. A stale baseline or non-monotonic scope sequence can therefore persist a receipt while returning accepted=false/rollback. Required fix: move full revision/replay/scope-sequence/history validation inside the same repository transaction before anchor.prepare/DB commit/promote, with tests proving repository count, anchor head, proposal and stores remain unchanged on validation failure. Existing compute_sm3_digest remains a documented SHA-256 stand-in and must not be described as real SM3.
